theorem_title: Uniform standard-Borel-target consequence of Haar amplification
formal_statement:
theorem ModNullUniversality.haar_amplification
    (K : ModNullUniversality.CompactMetrizableHaarGroup)
    (F : ModNullUniversality.StandardBorelEquivalence)
    (hF : Nonempty F.Carrier) :
    ∃ Q : ModNullUniversality.StandardBorelEquivalence,
      ∀ H : Subgroup K.Carrier, MeasurableSet (H : Set K.Carrier) →
        ∀ C : Set K.Carrier, MeasurableSet C → K.haar C = 1 →
          ModNullUniversality.BorelReducible
            (fun x y : C => ModNullUniversality.CosetRelation K H x.val y.val) F.rel →
          ModNullUniversality.BorelReducible (ModNullUniversality.CosetRelation K H) Q.rel := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Fix a compact metrizable group $K$ with normalized Haar probability and a Borel equivalence relation $F$ on a nonempty standard Borel space. There is one Borel equivalence relation $Q$ on a standard Borel space, chosen before the subgroup or domain, such that for every Borel subgroup $H\le K$ and every Borel Haar-conull $C\subseteq K$,

$$E_H^K\mathbin{\upharpoonright}C\leq_B F
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad E_H^K\leq_B Q.$$

This target records the uniform standard-Borel consequence of the manuscript's Lemmas 3.1–3.2. Those lemmas provide the almost-everywhere power as such a target. The statement here does not identify $Q$ with a separately formalized topological $L^0$ space. No abelian hypothesis or invariance of $C$ is imposed. The original reduction and the resulting global reduction are allowed to depend on $H$ and $C$.
source: Universality modulo null sets in the Borel hierarchy, user-supplied unpublished manuscript dated 9 November 2026; SHA-256 48745c75427f83370292c2e4cf91ec06377e80472252db0182599edcd05e2d97, Lemmas 3.1–3.2, lines 135–236, specifically the uniform target consequence in lines 218–220. The source almost-everywhere power is also discussed by B. Tsirelson, arXiv:math/0508414, Section 1, p. 3. https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0508414

For every object $K$ consisting of a carrier group $G$, a compact metrizable topology on $G$ for which multiplication and inversion are continuous, a measurable-space structure equal to the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of that topology, and a measure $\mu$ on $G$ satisfying $\mu(G)=1$ and the Haar-measure assumptions of finiteness on compact sets, left invariance, and positive measure for every nonempty open set, and for every object $F$ consisting of a carrier $Y$ with a measurable-space structure admitting a compatible Polish topology, a relation $R_F\subseteq Y\times Y$ that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, and measurability of its graph in the product measurable space, assume additionally that $Y$ is nonempty. Then there exists an object $Q$ consisting of a carrier $Z$ with a measurable-space structure admitting a compatible Polish topology and a reflexive, symmetric, transitive relation $R_Q\subseteq Z\times Z$ with measurable graph, such that the following holds for every subgroup $H\leq G$ whose underlying subset is Borel measurable and every Borel measurable subset $C\subseteq G$ satisfying $\mu(C)=1$: if there exists a measurable map $f:C\to Y$, where $C$ has the measurable structure induced from $G$, such that for all $x,y\in C$, $x^{-1}y\in H$ if and only if $R_F(f(x),f(y))$, then there exists a measurable map $g:G\to Z$ such that for all $x,y\in G$, $x^{-1}y\in H$ if and only if $R_Q(g(x),g(y))$. The single object $Q$ is chosen after $K$, $F$, and the nonemptiness hypothesis and before $H$, $C$, and the assumed map $f$; it must serve for all of those subsequent choices, while the concluding map $g$ may depend on them. Neither map is required to be injective or surjective. No commutativity of $G$, normality or closedness of $H$, or invariance of $C$ under the relation is assumed. The quantifiers include singleton groups and singleton $Y$, the identity subgroup and the whole group as $H$, and $C=G$; the condition $\mu(C)=1$ excludes $C=\varnothing$. For any $H,C$ for which the stated measurable map $f$ does not exist, the implication imposes no concluding reduction for that pair.
